newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tabacalera Aldeasa buy to boost retail.
newsitem.headline: Tabacalera Aldeasa buy to boost retail.

text.p: Tabacalera's buy of 20 percent of duty-free shop operator Aldeasa will bolster the tobacco maker's presence in the retail market although the benefits of the deal much depend on the final price, analysts said on Wednesday.

Spain's Stock Market Commission CNMV said on Wednesday Tabacalera would buy 20 percent of state-owned Aldeasa. In a separate announcement, state holding firm Seppa said it would sell the other 80 percent stake to institutions in September.

"Aldeasa is a great company and highly profitable and the adquisition of a stake is a good investment for Tabacalera and falls within the company's strategy to strengthen distribution," an analyst said.
Tabacalera has monopoly rights to distribute its tobacco products to the state-run estancos, which are outlets for tobacco and stamps, but it has been seen as lacking in reach in the retail market.
Aldeasa has extensive retail market. It manages 100 duty-free stores in 16 Spanish airports and is present in the airports of Peru, Venezuela, Chile, Portugal and Morrocco.
Tabacalera said it would pay 11.34 billion pesetas for the deal plus an additional fee related to the price of the sale of the 80 percent stake to institutions.

"The price is a key factor and it seems to me that Tabacalera will have to buy a premium over the price of the institutional sale, which could make the operation less attractive," another Spanish broker said.

A price of the order of 11 billion pesetas for 20 percent of Aldeasa would mean a price to earnings (PE) ratio of 10, given that the duty-free stores earned more than five million pesetas net in 1996.
"To buy at a PE of 10 would be excellent," said a foreign bank analyst, adding that the final price would more likely be situated at a PE of 13 times.

But despite the price worries, the bourse welcomed news of the purchase. At 1215 GMT, Tabacalera shares were up 90 pesetas, or 1.17 percent at 7,770, outpacing the overall bourse which was up 13.78 points, or 0.21 percent, at 6,557.59.
Tabacalera itself emphasised that the investment in Aldeasa would help add profitability for its shareholders.
The purchase represents "a unique opportunity to diversify in a sector which is already known...centred in a high-growth segment," Tabacalera said in a statement.

Although duty-free business may suffer in Europe if tax-free sales to travellers within the European Union are scrapped by the the turn of the century, the location and clientele of the duty-free shops continues to offer high profitability.
Duty free stores sell four times more than a normal store, and if there were no restrictions on sales after 2000, any buyer would have to pay an PE of 15 or more, one analyst said.
In the last three years Aldeasa's net profit rose 25 percent on average a year as air traffic volumes, and thus passengers, increased markedly, Tabacalera said.
